Subject: Unexpected charge on MAR invoice — request to hold payment

Hi Marcus,

We reviewed our March statement and noticed a ~$12,400 charge attributed to 'continuous-batching' tokens that doesn't match our usage patterns. Attached is our invoice and a short export from our metering showing the anomalous spike on 2026-03-12.

We're preparing a payment for the remainder of the balance but have placed the wire into escrow until this is reconciled. Can you confirm whether Redwood has any known ingestion/connector issue on that date, and advise next steps for a formal credit if this is on your side?

Thanks — please loop in accounting if you need evidence.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Director of Finance
Stellus Health

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the export. I’m sorry for the disruption and the escrowed wire — we'll prioritize this.

Quick updates:
- I’ve asked our metering team to pull ingestion logs and request traces for your account around 2026-03-12.
- Ben (billing) will calculate the disputed token delta and propose a credit schedule (goodwill vs service credit).
- Soojin (support/ops) will check for connector anomalies or unusually long KV-cache retention that could explain the spike.

Can you confirm the last four digits of the invoice so our accounting system maps it correctly? Also if you have a concise CSV of the rows you referenced, please share to speed reconciliation.

I’ll aim to get an initial estimate and ETA within two business days. Apologies again — we want to make this right quickly.

— Marcus
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: preliminary credit calc + accounting impact (Stellus)

Marcus / Soojin — posting the short internal calc here so we can be aligned before replying to Elena: 

- Raw disputed token count (per customer export): 1,235,400 tokens
- Expected baseline (rolling weekly average): 183,000 tokens
- Delta attributed to anomaly: 1,052,400 tokens
- Price per 1k tokens (contract): $0.45 per 1k => Credit amount: (1,052,400 / 1000) * 0.45 = $473.58 (note: this looks too small — double-check decimals in customer export)

I pulled meter logs — looks like the customer export is in token-units, but our metering reports raw token-words vs token-chunks. I suspect a scaling factor (x1,000) misapplied when the customer exported from their billing CSV. If it's x1,000, disputed credit would be ~$473,580 which matches the customer note (~$12k doesn't match either).

Action items:
- Soojin: confirm whether ingestion trace indicates repeat retries (retries would inflate token counts) — see trace id ST-20260312-77 (linked in Drive).
- Marcus: propose we offer a provisional goodwill credit of $15,000 to release escrow while we finish the full reconciliation. That covers short-term customer impact and reduces churn risk.
- Finance: if full reconciliation proves smaller than provisional, we can adjust on next invoice; if larger, we'll follow normal dispute process and issue credit memo.

I’ll prepare the sample credit memo template and send to accounting for pre-approval.

Attachment: payment_trace_escrow.png (screenshot of payment status)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@stellushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, finance@stellushealth.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Stellus Health — billing reconciliation & escrowed payment release

Hi Elena — quick update from our side and a proposal to get your payment cleared: 

1) We ran initial meter reconciliations and found inconsistent token scaling in the CSV export you sent; our preliminary parsing indicates the export multiplied token chunks by 1,000. We're doing a full pass but that accounts for the large disparity.

2) To avoid further disruption we propose a provisional goodwill credit of $15,000 to be applied immediately as a one-time credit memo. This will allow you to release the escrowed payment for the remainder of the balance.

3) Next steps:
   - If you accept the provisional credit, we'll issue a credit memo (CM-2026-0789) today and notify accounting.
   - We will complete the full reconciliation by 2026-08-10; if the final reconciliation results in a larger owed credit, we will issue the additional credit; if smaller, we will roll the difference into your next invoice.

Please reply with acceptance and the invoice last four digits so our billing team can map it and issue the memo. Apologies again for the inconvenience — appreciate your patience.

Best,
Marcus Lin
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
